title: Reassembly of a single ordered Cech row from subset coordinates
statement: For A a commutative ring, r a natural number, f:Fin r to A, and an integer cochain complex J of module sheaves on Spec A, use the explicit subset coordinates and insertion of [def-sc-principal-open-cech-subset-insertion] and the ordered double complex K of [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Let p be any natural number, q and n any integers with p+q=n, and w an element of the p-th ordered tuple product for the restriction of J^q. Let s be a subset coordinate family in degree n. Assume s vanishes on every nonempty subset whose cardinality is not p+1. Assume for every nonempty S of cardinality p+1 that w evaluated at its increasing enumeration is heterogeneously equal to the section transport of s(S), using coefficient J^(n+1-card(S)). Then applying the inverse extension isomorphism to w and including bidegree (p,q) into total degree n equals explicit subset insertion of s. The heterogeneous equality only accounts for the equal coefficient degrees and tuple-intersection presentations; the total degree equation forces q=n+1-card(S).

source.place: Tag 01FG, ordered differential and tuple product preceding Definition 20.23.2; Tags 08C0 (equation 20.40.0.1) and 08C1, alternating Cech totalization. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01FG and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C1.

proof.text: Expand insertion as its finite sum over nonempty subsets. The support hypothesis removes every summand outside the finite filter of subsets of cardinality p+1. Expand w as the sum of its tuple singletons and use additivity of the extension inverse and total inclusion.

Use Finset.sum_bij to identify the filtered subsets with increasing (p+1)-tuples. The forward map is orderEmbOfFin; injectivity follows by equality of ranges. For surjectivity take the finite image of a tuple, prove its cardinality p+1, and use orderEmbOfFin_unique to identify its enumeration.

In each summand the subset cardinality gives p=card(S)-1 and the total-degree equality gives q=n+1-card(S). Substitute these equalities, turn the supplied HEq into equality, and expand principalSubsetInsertOne. The summands agree definitionally, including all degree proof witnesses.

lean.statement:
theorem principalSubsetRowReassembly
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (J : CochainComplex (Spec (.of A)).Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ) (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ) :
    let V := principalSubsetUnion A r f
    let U : Fin r → V.toScheme.Opens := fun i ↦ V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f i)
    let K := (alternatingCechDoubleFunctor U).obj (principalSubsetRestriction A r f J)
    let H := forget₂
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) AddCommGrpCat
    let P := alternatingCechModulePresheaf.obj ((principalSubsetRestriction A r f J).X q)
    let L := alternatingCechComplex U P
    let e : (K.X (p : ℤ)).X q ≅ L.X p :=
      L.extendXIso ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat rfl
    ∀ (hdeg : ComplexShape.π (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ((p : ℤ), q) = n)
      (w : L.X p) (s : principalSubsetCoordinates A r f J n),
      (∀ S : {S : Finset (Fin r) // S.Nonempty}, S.val.card ≠ p + 1 → s S = 0) →
      (∀ (S : {S : Finset (Fin r) // S.Nonempty}) (hcard : S.val.card = p + 1),
        HEq (w (S.val.orderEmbOfFin hcard))
          ((principalSubsetSectionTransport A r f
            (J.X (n + 1 - (S.val.card : ℤ))) S).hom (s S))) →
      (H.map (e.inv ≫ K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (p : ℤ) q n hdeg)) w =
        principalSubsetInsertion A r f J n s
